problem: Existing audio-visual navigation (AVN) methods fuse audio and vision by naive concatenation and assume binaural cues are always reliable; auxiliary geometric tasks are used only as training objectives and do not inform fusion at test time. Performance degrades under reverberation, multipath, and unheard sound categories.
motivation: In complex acoustics binaural cues are intermittently unreliable, and unheard sounds shift the audio feature distribution, so agents drift toward spurious directions. Humans assess how trustworthy a sound is and lean on vision when it is unclear, so the agent should calibrate its trust in audio dynamically.
key_idea: Learn an audio-derived reliability cue via heteroscedastic Gaussian NLL geometric proxy supervision (distance and azimuth), and use it through a soft sigmoid gate to modulate visual features before the recurrent policy.
insight: Ablations show that replacing MSE with heteroscedastic NLL for the auxiliary distance loss improves results (Replica Unheard SR 47.7 to 51.9), so learning observation-dependent dispersion beats rigid metric regression. Adding the RAGM gate gives further gains (Replica Unheard SR 51.9 to 53.1, Mp3D Heard SNA 29.4 to 33.2). The gate is conditioned on the geometric embedding, which shares its encoder with the uncertainty heads, so no geometric labels are needed at inference. Gains are larger on Replica than on Matterport3D.
method: Acoustic Geometry Reasoner (AGR): shared encoder over CNN audio features f_a yields a latent z_geo, feeding a distance head, an azimuth head and a projection head.
Probabilistic distance head: predicts Gaussian (mu, sigma^2) for geodesic distance trained with heteroscedastic NLL; variance serves as a proxy for acoustic reliability.
Azimuth head: regresses relative azimuth with a wrapped Smooth-L1 loss to handle angular periodicity (the text also mentions cross-entropy in the objective, an inconsistency).
Projection head: maps z_geo to g_t in R^{D_v}, aligned with the visual feature dimension and carrying direction and reliability information.
RAGM: mask m_t = Sigmoid(MLP(g_t)) in (0,1)^{D_v}, and modulated visual feature f'_v = f_v ⊙ m_t (element-wise gate).
Policy: concatenate raw audio f_a with modulated visual f'_v, then a GRU gives s_t for actor-critic; trained end-to-end with PPO plus lambda * (L_dist + L_ang).

setting.backbone: CNN audio and depth encoders + GRU actor-critic with AGR/RAGM modules (trained from scratch, PPO)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces RL training only: 48M steps on Replica, 60M steps on Matterport3D; auxiliary geometric labels (GT distance/azimuth) used in training only; no extra data
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (episodes limited to 500 steps)
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT geodesic distance/azimuth used only for training-time auxiliary supervision)

numbers.backbone: CNN + GRU, PPO with AGR + RAGM
numbers.extra: multiple heard sounds; all 102 sounds in train/val/test

numbers_note: Split names are not stated explicitly; 'test' was assumed for the standard SoundSpaces protocol. The Mp3D ablation table reports AV-Nav Unheard SR 33.5 / SPL 21.9 / SNA 10.4, which differs from the main table's 34.5 / 25.0 / 12.7. Ablation variants (+AGR MSE, +AGR NLL) are in Tables 2-3 and not listed above.
results: RAVN beats AV-Nav on all four settings. Replica Unheard SR is 53.1 vs 47.3 and SPL 40.3 vs 36.8; Replica Heard SR is 97.0 vs 93.0. On Matterport3D, Heard SR is 70.9 vs 68.8 and Unheard SR 35.6 vs 34.5, so gains there are smaller.
limitations: Compared only against older baselines (AV-Nav and a few from 2020); no recent AVN methods and no multi-seed variance reported.
Reliability is only implicitly used (no analysis of the gate values or calibration of sigma); the gain on Matterport3D Unheard is small (+1.1 SR).
Simulation only; no real-robot or severe-noise/degraded-sensor evaluation, and the paper is inconsistent about the azimuth loss (Smooth-L1 vs cross-entropy).
compares_to: Gan et al. (Look, Listen, and Act)
